sender.en: A stranger on Facebook, then a “courier” and a “police officer”

name.en: Facebook message about a grant or prize that needs “delivery fees”

how.en: A stranger messages you on Facebook to congratulate you on a prize or an international grant worth thousands of dollars. An “agent” says it will be delivered by a courier company, but first you must pay delivery fees. When the package doesn’t come, someone posing as a police officer asks for more money to release it. A man in Toledo District lost BZ$745 this way.

text.en: A stranger on Facebook says you have won a prize or a large grant.
An “agent” or courier asks you to pay a delivery fee, often in several deposits.
Someone posing as a police officer or official asks for more to release the money.

Congratulations!! Your name was approved for the International Empowerment Grant of US$50,000. Your package is ready with our courier agent. Contact him to pay the delivery and clearance fee so it can reach you in Belize this week.

en: facebook message said i won a grant
pay a delivery fee to receive my grant money
courier agent asking for clearance fee for prize package
police officer asking for money to release my prize
international grant approved message on facebook
You won something you never entered.
You must pay fees before receiving money.
A “police officer” or official joins in to ask for more money.
Stop replying and don’t send any money.
Real grants and prizes never charge delivery fees.
If you paid, contact your bank and report it to the police.

sources.title: Online Scam: Belize Man loses $745 after replying to unknown account on Facebook
